children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by accessing the official assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I can see we need to start by checking information about your child. Let me ask you some key questions:

**First, I need to know about your child:**

1. **How old is your child?** (Or if you have multiple children, how old are they?)

This will help me determine which rules apply to your situation. Child Benefit has different eligibility rules depending on whether a child is:
- **Under 16** years old
- **16-19** years old (with specific education/training requirements)
- **20 or over** (generally not eligible)

Please tell me your child's age(s), and I'll guide you through the rest of the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 9 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thanks for that information. So we're assessing eligibility for **Alex, who is 9 years old**. Since Alex is under 16, he qualifies as a potential qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes.

Now let me move forward with the next checks:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check the next requirement:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

At age 9, I expect he's not in full-time work, but I need to confirm this for the records. Is Alex:
- Not working in paid employment, or
- Working less than 24 hours per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 9, so he's still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's what I expected. Alex is in primary school and not working, so he definitely meets this requirement.

Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now the next requirement:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, is Alex receiving any of these benefits as a claimant in their own name:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

For a 9-year-old in primary school, the answer is likely no, but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex NOT in a disqualifying apprenticeship?**

At age 9, this is straightforward - is Alex in any apprenticeship program at all? Or is he just in regular primary school education?

(Note: Different apprenticeship types in different parts of the UK have different rules, but given Alex's age, I expect he's simply in regular schooling.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's just in regular primary school - he's far too young for any apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That makes sense. Alex is in regular primary school, so he's definitely not in any apprenticeship. Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now we need to check **your residency status** as the claimant. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit.

I can see there are several paths that can make someone eligible. Let me ask you the most straightforward question first:

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

If you do, that's the simplest path to meeting the residency requirement. However, if your situation is more complex (for example, you have EU Settlement Scheme status, or you're a Crown servant living abroad), please let me know and I can explore those options with you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK - I live abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since you live abroad, we need to explore which specific circumstances might still allow you to qualify. Let me ask you some follow-up questions:

**1. Are you a Crown servant (or family member of one) living abroad in certain qualifying countries?**
   - This includes British diplomatic staff, military personnel, or other Crown servants posted overseas

**2. Or do you have EU Settlement Scheme status?** This could be:
   - Settled status
   - Pre-settled status (with specific work, study, or financial circumstances)

**3. Alternatively, is there another specific reason you're living abroad that might be relevant?**

Please tell me more about your situation so I can determine if any of these paths apply to you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or military personnel, and I don't have EU Settlement Scheme status. I just live abroad with my family.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I appreciate you being straightforward about your situation.

Based on what you've told me:
- You live abroad
- You don't have Crown servant status
- You don't have EU Settlement Scheme status
- You're simply living abroad with your family

Unfortunately, this means you don't meet any of the residency paths that would qualify you for Child Benefit. The main eligibility requirement is that you normally live in the UK, or fall into one of the specific exceptions (like Crown servant status or EU Settlement Scheme status).

Let me confirm this is the correct outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me provide you with the final eligibility assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Complete - **NOT ELIGIBLE**

I'm sorry to deliver this result, but based on the official eligibility rules, **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

**Why you're not eligible:**

While Alex fully meets the requirements as a qualifying child (he's 9 years old, in school, not working, and not receiving benefits), **you do not meet the UK residency requirements**. Child Benefit is only available to:
- People who normally live in the UK, OR
- People in specific circumstances such as:
  - Crown servants posted abroad
  - People with EU Settlement Scheme status (settled or pre-settled with qualifying criteria)
  - People living in certain designated countries

Since you live abroad without these qualifying circumstances, you cannot claim Child Benefit for Alex.

**What you might do:**

1. **If your circumstances change** - If you move back to the UK, you could reapply for Child Benefit
2. **Check for other support** - There may be other benefits or allowances available in the country where you're living
3. **Contact HMRC directly** - If you believe your situation is more complex or there are qualifying circumstances I haven't covered, you can contact HMRC on 0300 200 3100

**Helpful link:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

I'm sorry I couldn't bring better news, but I wanted to be clear about why you don't qualify under the current rules.

Therefore, while Alex meets the child-related requirements, the claimant does not meet the residency requirements necessary to claim Child Benefit for him.
